narrative: New England fell to SEA 10-13. The offense posted -0.11 EPA/play (42% success rate) while the defense allowed 0.07 EPA/play. Turnover margin was -3.

good: Red zone defense held Seattle to just 1 TD on 3 opportunities—at least we weren't getting torched in the most critical situations.
DaQuan Jones joining the defensive line provides some reinforcement in the trenches as we navigate the injury fallout.
bad: A.J. Brown's high ankle sprain lands him on IR for at least four games, removing our most explosive receiving weapon at perhaps the worst possible time.
Third-down efficiency was a disaster: 5 for 16 on offense while Seattle converted 2 for 11—we couldn't sustain drives when we needed to, and couldn't force them into obvious passing situations.
ugly: Minus-3 turnover margin in a three-point loss is exactly how you doom yourself; we coughed it up at critical moments and couldn't create takeaways to compensate.

playerOfTheGame.reason: Had the team's best (though still net-negative) win probability contribution at -3% in a tough game offensively.

fanTake: Well, that's the kind of loss that stings in ways that go beyond the scoreboard. Down 10-13 to Seattle in a game we absolutely should have won, we managed the impressive feat of turning the ball over three more times than we forced them to—which is a fancy way of saying we beat ourselves. The offense couldn't find its footing (negative EPA per play will do that to you), the defense couldn't tighten up when it mattered most, and R. Stevenson, our Player of the Game by WPA, somehow managed negative win probability added, which tells you everything you need to know about how this one went. And now we're doing it all without A.J. Brown for the next month, minimum. Fun times.
